evidence: Plaut. Asin. 30: cavē mihi mendācī quicquam
terms.comment: mendācī is the old genitive, as in Plautus.

terms.gloss: lying; as a noun, a liar

phrases.latin: dīc obsecrō hercle sēriō quod tē rogem, cavē mihi mendācī quicquam
phrases.english: for heaven’s sake, answer me seriously what I ask you, and no lies, mind

phrases.latin: hoc juvat et mellī est, nōn mentiar
phrases.english: I won’t lie: I love it, it’s honey to me

phrases.latin: cum mendācī hominī nē vērum quidem dīcentī crēdere soleāmus
phrases.english: since we do not believe a liar even when he tells the truth

sources: Lewis & Short: mentior · Lewis & Short: mendacium · Lewis & Short: mendax
